papers.title: Being-H0.5: Scaling Human-Centric Robot Learning for Cross-Embodiment Generalization
papers.abstract: We present Being-H0.5, a Vision-Language-Action foundation model for cross-embodiment generalization. To address morphological diversity and data scarcity, we propose a human-centric learning paradigm treating human interaction traces as a universal ``mother tongue'' for physical skills. We curate a 35,000-hour embodied pre-training corpus spanning human and 30 robotic embodiments. Central to our approach is a unified action space that maps human hand motion and heterogeneous robot controls into semantically aligned slots, enabling low-resource robots to bootstrap from human and high-resource platforms. Built on this foundation, we develop unified sequence modeling and multi-task pre-training to jointly learn from human demonstrations and robot trajectories. Architecturally, Being-H0.5 extends conventional Mixture-of-Transformers with a novel Mixture-of-Flow, which separates shared motor primitives from embodiment-specific action experts. For real-world stability, we introduce Manifold-Preserving Gating to mitigate sensory shift and Universal Async Chunking for chunked control across varying latencies and control rates. Being-H0.5 achieves state-of-the-art results on LIBERO and RoboCasa, and demonstrates strong cross-embodiment performance across five real robot platforms.

papers.title: MoDex: Towards Universal Multi-Object Dexterous Grasping
papers.abstract: Multi-object grasping is a fundamental yet challenging problem, constrained by data collection costs, varying spatial layouts, and the need for broad generalization. To address these challenges, we propose MoDex, a data-efficient framework that provides the first unified solution for universal multi-object dexterous grasping across diverse spatial layouts. MoDex accomplishes this by formulating the task as a single-step decision problem of learning residual corrections to a reference trajectory, and introducing a spatially adaptive dual-strategy that performs single-shot grasping for proximal objects and sequential interaction for separated objects. Extensive evaluations show that MoDex significantly outperforms baselines in proximal configurations, achieving 64.17% success on unseen objects, and uniquely succeeds in separated layouts where prior methods struggle. Further experiments demonstrate its generalization across robot embodiments, scalability and zero-shot sim-to-real deployment through a vision-based policy trained solely on simulation data.

papers.title: EVOLVE: Egocentric Vision-based Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via Demonstration Editing
papers.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires long-horizon coordination between locomotion and object interaction, as well as robust adaptation to diverse objects and noisy real-world observations. Recent approaches have shown promising results by learning loco-manipulation policies from reference motions or task-specific rewards, but they often struggle to generalize across objects. We propose \textbf{\textsc{Evolve}}, a framework for learning egocentric vision-based humanoid loco-manipulation through simulation-based demonstration editing and hierarchical visuomotor policy training. Given a single successful demonstration, our method adapts it to diverse objects by applying structured transformations to robot keypoint trajectories. These edited trajectories are executed by a task-agnostic low-level whole-body controller that tracks future target poses of sparse body keypoints. We then train a high-level visuomotor policy from the successful edited rollouts to enable real-world deployment. In simulation, our method generalizes across substantial object variations in size, shape, pose, and initialization, outperforming representative reference-based and reference-free baselines. We further deploy the learned policy zero-shot on real-world tasks. These results suggest that combining demonstration editing with hierarchical visuomotor control is a scalable strategy for transferring humanoid loco-manipulation skills from a single demonstration to diverse real-world objects.

papers.title: General Humanoid Whole-Body Control via Pretraining and Fast Adaptation
papers.abstract: Learning a general whole-body controller for humanoid robots remains challenging due to the diversity of motion distributions, the difficulty of fast adaptation, and the need for robust balance in high-dynamic scenarios. Existing approaches often require task-specific training or suffer from performance degradation when adapting to new motions. In this paper, we present \textbf{FAST}, a general humanoid whole-body control framework that enables \underline{F}ast \underline{A}daptation and \underline{S}table Motion \underline{T}racking. FAST introduces Parseval-Guided Residual Policy Adaptation, which learns a lightweight delta action policy under orthogonality and KL constraints, enabling efficient adaptation to out-of-distribution motions while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. To further improve physical robustness, we propose Center-of-Mass-Aware Control, which incorporates CoM-related observations and objectives to enhance balance when tracking challenging reference motions. Extensive experiments in simulation and real-world deployment demonstrate that FAST consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in robustness, adaptation efficiency, and generalization. papers.title: RealDexUMI: A Wearable Universal Manipulation Interface for Dexterous Robot Learning
papers.abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation requires demonstrations that preserve fine hand-object interactions while remaining executable at deployment. Existing pipelines either lose deployable dexterity through retargeting or embodiment conversion, or rely on robot-specific teleoperation that is costly to scale and often lacks intuitive, contact-aware control for dexterous data collection. We present RealDexUMI, a wearable universal manipulation interface built around a shared dexterous end-effector module that integrates a lightweight dexterous hand, in-hand vision, and fingertip tactile sensing. A palm-side isomorphic teleoperation glove maps human finger inputs to robot-hand joint commands, enabling real-time, retargeting-free, intuitive, and precise hand control. The shared hand and sensing modules yield zero-gap end-effector data, with matched in-hand observations, tactile signals, contacts, and hand actions between collection and deployment. Across eight real-robot tasks spanning fine-grained, contact-rich, long-horizon, and bimanual manipulation, policies trained on RealDexUMI data achieve an average success rate of 88.75%, generalize to unseen initial poses, and transfer across three embodiments.
